stem: A client recently diagnosed with diabetes says, “I feel overwhelmed and I’m not sure how this will fit into my life.” Which response by the nurse is best?

options.A: Acknowledge the client’s feelings, use open-ended questions to identify specific concerns and supports, and collaborate on manageable next steps rather than assuming a fixed emotional stage.
options.B: Explain that every client progresses through the same predictable sequence of denial, anger, bargaining, depression, and acceptance before diabetes education can be effective.
options.C: Redirect the conversation to glucose targets because emotional reactions are not part of routine diabetes care.
options.D: Reassure the client that adjustment should be complete within a few weeks and that ongoing psychosocial support is usually unnecessary.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend person-centered psychosocial care as part of routine diabetes management. Health care professionals should create a supportive environment for emotional disclosure, validate the individual’s experience, use open-ended questions and empathetic listening, assess available resources and barriers, and collaborate on coping and self-management goals. Current guidance does not require a universal stage-based adjustment sequence. B imposes a rigid model not supported as a required clinical pathway. C ignores psychosocial well-being, which is a critical component of diabetes care. D creates an unsupported timetable and may minimize persistent support needs.
educational_objective: Support psychological adjustment to a new chronic illness diagnosis with validation, open-ended assessment, person-centered communication, and collaborative coping/self-management planning rather than imposing a fixed emotional-stage model.
source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
source_document_title: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026; Comprehensive Medical Evaluation and Assessment of Comorbidities: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_locator: Section 5 Psychosocial Care, Recommendation 5.42 and accompanying text — psychosocial care is part of routine medical care; create supportive space for emotional disclosure, validate experiences, use open-ended questions and empathetic listening, collaborative goal setting and coping strategies. Section 4 Recommendations 4.1–4.2 — person-centered, strength-based, nonjudgmental communication and active listening
source_claim_supported: Current diabetes standards support individualized, person-centered psychosocial assessment and emotional support during diagnosis and other changes rather than assuming that every client follows a fixed or time-limited adjustment sequence.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — use therapeutic communication, assess coping and support systems, and assist clients adapting to changes in health status
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — adjustment to a new chronic illness diagnosis
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item because its generic denial/grief/adaptation wording risks teaching a rigid stage model as a predictable clinical sequence. The final item tests the current evidence-based nursing approach: validate the client’s experience, assess concerns and resources with open-ended communication, and collaborate on individualized coping and self-management support.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against ADA Standards of Care 2026 Sections 5 and 4. The standards explicitly support validation, open-ended questions, empathetic listening, psychosocial screening, and collaborative person-centered care.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A consists only of supported therapeutic actions. The final item deliberately rejects a mandatory stage sequence or fixed adjustment timeline because current standards emphasize individualized assessment and support.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; it uses person-centered psychosocial care and therapeutic communication.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; a universal predictable stage sequence should not be imposed as a prerequisite for effective care.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; psychosocial well-being is part of routine diabetes care and affects self-management.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; no universal short timetable for adjustment is established and ongoing support may be needed.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A combines validation, assessment, and collaborative planning without unsupported assumptions about how adjustment must proceed.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are realistic nursing responses to the same disclosure and differ by therapeutic quality rather than factual trivia.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity is directly aligned because the construct is therapeutic communication and adaptation to a change in health status.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked stage-model overgeneralization, person-centered communication, emotional disclosure, support-system assessment, time-course claims, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
